objective: Quantify whether cross-destination tail packing and a 1024-bit PWP source jointly remove the three balanced M143 bottlenecks without changing the event multiset.

architecture_assumptions.stable_pack_order: same row, destination block then increasing source

required_rtl_admission: VCS/SVA proof that cross-block packing preserves every source and destination tuple, including zero and tail rows.
Conflict-aware four-update correction module with exact same-destination combining or explicitly banked destinations.
PWP1024 frontend RTL and a macro bandwidth/energy sensitivity envelope.
Cycle replay with measured conflict stalls and finite endpoint latency before promoting any ratio.
required_review_questions: Does mosaic packing conserve the ordered destination/source tuple multiset rather than only the total popcount?
Does the recurrence incorrectly grant four arbitrary destination updates per cycle without conflict cost?
Are PWP1024 beat counts exact for 96 lanes at signed width 8 through 11?
Are compact256 and dualrow512 frozen baselines compared on the same heldout workload and same-clock boundary?
Could descriptor tag growth, update banking, or a realizable 1024-bit macro erase the cycle opportunity?
